core_obligations: Retain the full nonlinear marked-tree contraction as an uncounted local input proof, while identifying the genuinely new derivative/remainder mechanism.
Represent the derivative by marked rightmost leaves and symmetrize it into a sum over all leaves.

Show the quadratic remainder vanishes unless at least two nonsingleton leaves differ under the product optimal coupling; control the remaining probability and exact tree-weight decay. Establish Hamming-Wasserstein monotonicity for arbitrary one-site marginals through symmetric recombination couplings. Interpolate the particle law and the nonlinear evolution of the empirical law; cancel first-order generator terms and integrate the exponentially decaying second-order residual to obtain a bound uniform in time.

proof_roadmap.step: Wild trees, singleton cancellation and the exact pair-survival statistic give the previously selected two-solution contraction; it is supporting proof, not the new counted claim.
A marked derivative-tree identity and leaf symmetrization expose a second-order cancellation requiring two differing nonsingleton leaves, giving a decaying quadratic error.
Symmetrically exchange both children in a coupling to preserve the average Hamming cost and obtain W nonexpansion for arbitrary laws.

Split empirical sampling, dynamic consistency and initial error; interpolate and use Q(S_s(q))=bar S_s(q)Q(q), so only second-order particle increments remain. Their e^(-Ds)/N contribution integrates uniformly in t.

difficulty_reason: After elementary finite ODE, coupling and sampling tools are supplied, the decisive new obligation is a uniform-in-time finite-particle consistency estimate for a nonlinear recombination flow. It needs a marked-tree representation of its time-dependent derivative, two-leaf cancellation for a decaying quadratic remainder, and an interpolation in which the exact empirical generator identity cancels the first variation. These steps distinguish the result from the earlier H2 two-solution contraction and from a fixed-time Gronwall propagation bound. The full retained chain is a coordinated research-level quantitative propagation-of-chaos argument; its final initial-distance substitution or the canonical CLT rate is not being counted as additional difficulty.
